meta.title: Game 4 Adjusting Entries Factory (US Principles of Accounting)
meta.note: Perpetual inventory, allowance method, fiscal year ends December 31. For closing and income-tax entries the player picks the main debit and credit accounts.

lv1.q: Insurance premium was debited to Insurance Expense when paid. Part of the coverage is still unused at year-end.
On July 1, paid $24,000 for two years of insurance and debited Insurance Expense. Defer the unexpired part at December 31.
Rent paid in advance was debited to Rent Expense. Part of it covers next year. Adjust at year-end.
Supplies purchased were debited to Supplies Expense. A count shows $350 of supplies still on hand.
An advertising campaign was paid in advance and debited to Advertising Expense. Part of the campaign runs next year.
Supplies on hand were $900 at the start of the year. No supplies were bought during the year. The year-end count shows $300 on hand. Record the supplies used.
Prepaid Insurance was set up when the premium was paid. One year of coverage has now expired.
Rent was paid in advance and debited to Prepaid Rent. Several months of that rent have now been used.
A year of advertising was prepaid and recorded as Prepaid Advertising. Part of it has now run.
A client paid in advance for services and the cash was credited to Unearned Revenue. The services have now been performed.
Cash received in advance was credited to Service Revenue. Some of the services have not yet been performed.
Rent received in advance was credited to Unearned Rent. Part of the rent period has now passed.
Rent received in advance was credited to Rent Revenue. Part of it covers next year's rent.
Customers prepaid annual membership fees, which were credited to Unearned Revenue. Part of the year has passed.
Interest has been earned on a note receivable but has not been received. Record it at year-end.
A tenant owes December rent that has not been billed or recorded.
Services were performed for a client but not yet billed or recorded.
Commissions were earned in December but not yet recorded or collected.
Employees have earned salaries that have not been paid at year-end.
Hourly workers earned wages during the last three days of the year. They will be paid next year.
Interest of $450 has built up on a note payable but has not been paid.
Electricity was used in December, but the bill has not yet arrived.
The employer's share of U.S. FICA tax on accrued wages has not been paid.
Record the year's depreciation on office equipment.
lv1.hint: Expense increase (debit) / Contra asset (accumulated depreciation) increase (credit)

lv1.q: Record the year's depreciation on the company's building.
lv1.hint: Expense increase (debit) / Contra asset (accumulated depreciation) increase (credit)

lv1.q: Record the year's depreciation on a delivery van.
lv1.hint: Expense increase (debit) / Contra asset (accumulated depreciation) increase (credit)

lv1.q: Record the year's depreciation on store furniture.
lv1.hint: Expense increase (debit) / Contra asset (accumulated depreciation) increase (credit)

lv1.q: Estimate bad debts as a percent of credit sales for the year. Record the adjustment.
An aging of Accounts Receivable shows $4,800 will probably not be collected. The allowance has no balance yet.
A customer's $400 account is declared uncollectible. Write it off using the allowance method.
A physical count shows less merchandise on hand than the perpetual records, cause unknown. Record the shrinkage.
The cash drawer holds $15 less than the register tape shows. The cause is unknown.
lv1.hint: Cash Over and Short increase (debit) / Asset decrease (credit)

lv1.q: The cash drawer holds $8 more than the register tape shows. The cause is unknown.
lv1.hint: Asset increase (debit) / Cash Over and Short increase (credit)

lv1.q: At year-end, Cash Over and Short has a debit balance. Close it to Income Summary.
lv1.hint: Income Summary (debit) / Cash Over and Short decrease (credit)

lv1.q: At year-end, Cash Over and Short has a credit balance. Close it to Income Summary.
lv1.hint: Cash Over and Short decrease (debit) / Income Summary (credit)

lv2.q:
On October 1, paid $18,000 for 24 months of insurance and debited Insurance Expense.
The year ends December 31. Defer the unexpired part.
lv2.calc: $18,000 ÷ 24 months = $750 per month. Oct-Dec used 3 months, so 21 months remain: $750 × 21 = $15,750.

lv2.q:
On November 1, paid $9,000 for six months of rent and debited Prepaid Rent.
The year ends December 31. Record the rent used.
lv2.calc: $9,000 ÷ 6 months = $1,500 per month. Nov and Dec are 2 months: $1,500 × 2 = $3,000.

lv2.q:
Supplies on hand were $1,400 on January 1. During the year, $3,900 of supplies were bought and debited to Supplies.
The year-end count shows $1,150 on hand. Record the supplies used.

On September 1, received $7,200 for 12 months of service and credited Unearned Revenue.
The year ends December 31. Record the revenue earned.
lv2.calc: $7,200 ÷ 12 months = $600 per month. Sept-Dec is 4 months: $600 × 4 = $2,400.

lv2.q:
On November 1, received $6,000 for six months of rent and credited Rent Revenue.
The year ends December 31. Defer the unearned part.
lv2.calc: $6,000 ÷ 6 months = $1,000 per month. Nov and Dec earned 2 months, so 4 months remain: $1,000 × 4 = $4,000.

lv2.q:
The company holds a $15,000 note receivable at 6% dated November 1.
The year ends December 31. Record the interest earned.

Salaries of $4,500 are paid every Friday for a five-day week.
December 31 falls on a Wednesday. Record the accrued salaries.
lv2.calc: $4,500 ÷ 5 days = $900 per day. Monday to Wednesday is 3 days: $900 × 3 = $2,700.

lv2.q:
The company borrowed $30,000 from the bank at 8% on September 1. Interest is paid when the loan matures.
The year ends December 31. Record the accrued interest.

Equipment cost $48,000, has a $6,000 salvage value, and a 7-year life.
Use straight-line depreciation. Record one year of depreciation.
lv2.hint: Expense increase (debit) / Contra asset (accumulated depreciation) increase (credit)

lv2.q:
A vehicle was bought on October 1 for $36,000. It has a $6,000 salvage value and a 5-year life.
Use straight-line depreciation. The year ends December 31. Record the depreciation.
lv2.hint: Expense increase (debit) / Contra asset (accumulated depreciation) increase (credit)

lv2.q:
Credit sales for the year were $400,000. The company estimates that 1.5% of credit sales will not be collected.
The allowance already has a $1,200 credit balance. Record bad debts using the percent of sales method.
lv2.calc: Percent of sales ignores the old balance. $400,000 × 1.5% = $6,000.

lv2.q:
Accounts Receivable is $120,000. The company estimates 4% will be uncollectible.
The allowance has a $1,300 credit balance. Record the adjustment using the percent of receivables method.
lv2.calc: Needed allowance = $120,000 × 4% = $4,800. Add to the $1,300 credit balance: $4,800 − $1,300 = $3,500.

lv2.q:
Accounts Receivable is $90,000. The company estimates 5% will be uncollectible.
The allowance has a $600 debit balance. Record the adjustment using the percent of receivables method.
lv2.calc: Needed allowance = $90,000 × 5% = $4,500 credit. Debit balance of $600 must be covered too: $4,500 + $600 = $5,100.

lv2.q:
Perpetual records show $86,400 of merchandise inventory. A physical count shows $83,150, cause unknown.
Record the inventory shrinkage.

Income before income taxes is $64,000. The tax rate is 21%.
No taxes have been recorded yet. Record the income tax for the year.

The company rents out space for $750 per month. The tenant has not paid November or December rent, and nothing is recorded.
Record the rent earned.

Total sales revenue for the year is $342,600.
Close the Sales Revenue account.
lv2.calc: The closing entry moves the full credit balance: $342,600.

lv2.q:
Over the year, Cash Over and Short recorded shortages of $85, $40, and $30, and overages of $25 and $55.
Close the account.
lv2.hint: Income Summary (debit) / Cash Over and Short decrease (credit)

lv2.q:
Revenues for the year were $215,000 and expenses were $168,500. All revenues and expenses are closed.
Close Income Summary.

The company declared dividends of $2,500 each quarter during the year.
Close the Dividends account.
